intro: Historians research, judge evidence and explain the past clearly, skills used in archives, museums and college teaching. The closest of the 25 careers below is Archivists, with an 85% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $64,550, which is 16% less than the $76,750 historians earn.
why_it_works: Your work means finding sources, weighing what they prove and writing for readers who were not there. O*NET rates complex problem solving at 3.38 out of 5 for historians. Archives, museums, libraries and postsecondary teaching rely on the same research habits. Every match needs no new degree. The skills to add are analyzing systems and data, teaching groups and serving the public.
tips: Show applied work, such as exhibits, oral histories or reports for agencies, not only publications.
Business Intelligence Analysts earn $120,230 for their broader BLS group and reward strong research skills.
College teaching pays more in some fields: anthropology and archeology teachers earn $99,650, or 30% more.

faq.q: What jobs can former historians do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Archivists (85%), postsecondary history teachers (81%) and Curators (80%), based on O*NET 31.0. History teachers in colleges earn $83,820, which is 9% more than the $76,750 historian median, while archives and museums usually pay a little less.

faq.q: Which careers for historians pay more?
faq.a: 17 of the 25 matches pay more than history work. Postsecondary law teachers earn $128,500 (67% more), economics teachers $123,920 (61% more) and anthropology and archeology teachers $99,650 (30% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. These roles usually need a doctorate in that subject.

faq.q: Do historians need another degree to change careers?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches usually need no more education than historians already have. A master's degree is the most common level, held by 84% of workers in the closest match, and many college roles expect a doctorate, which many historians already hold.

The skills that most often need work are systems analysis, instructing, systems evaluation and service orientation. Judgment and social perceptiveness already rate 3.12 out of 5 for historians in O*NET, so data analysis and teaching are the main steps for most moves.
